title: Open extension of an injective sheaf is acyclic for the proper right-hand map
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and let $A,B,C,D$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $k:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $i:C\hookrightarrow D$ be open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $r:A\to C$ and $p:B\to D$ be proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism] satisfying $pk=ir$. No Cartesian hypothesis is imposed. For every injective sheaf $J$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] [def-sp-injective-resolutions], the higher direct images of its extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] vanish:
$$R^qp_*(k_!J)=0\qquad(q>0),$$
where the higher direct images are those of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

source.place: Tag 0F7B, label lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, proof of case (b), claim R^q f_*(g_!′ J)=0 and geometric-fibre argument; open-immersion specialization

proof.text: Put $F=k_!J$ and write $F_{ab}$ for its underlying abelian sheaf. The additive group of the finite ring $\Lambda$ has a positive exponent $N$: for each element choose a positive integer killing it and multiply these finitely many integers. Thus $N1_\Lambda=0$ and $Nm=(N1_\Lambda)m=0$ on every $\Lambda$-module, including every section of $F$. In particular $F_{ab}$ is torsion. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison], exact forgetting identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of $R^qp_*F$ with $R^qp_*F_{ab}$. It therefore suffices to show the latter is zero. We will apply proper base change to abelian sheaves, never assert that $J_{ab}$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0D6J, lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded, (3); Tag 0F7B, case (b), torsion coefficients

proof.text: Form $V=B\times_D C$ with projections $b:V\to B$ and $s:V\to C$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The equation $pk=ir$ gives $t=(k,r):A\to V$. Because $i$ is an open immersion, $b$ identifies $V$ with the open $p^{-1}(C)$ of $B$, and $k(A)\subseteq p^{-1}(C)$; hence $t$ is the same open immersion as $k$, with this smaller target [def-weil-open-immersion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], $s$ is proper and thus separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $st=r$ is proper, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] implies that $t$ is proper. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] to $t$ (an open immersion is an immersion, with identity closed factor): it is a closed immersion as well. Write $W=V\setminus t(A)$ with its open subscheme structure; then $V=t(A)\amalg W$, with both pieces open and closed. No assertion that $A=V$ has been used.

Under the two-component equivalence of abelian sheaf categories [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-clopen-product], $t_!G$ corresponds to $(G,0)$: the unit $G\to t^{-1}t_!G$ of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] is induced by the identity on sections of etale objects factoring through $A$, so its stalk maps are the isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks]. The map $0\to (t_!G)|_W$ has zero stalks by the same node. Hence [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes both maps isomorphisms. These are natural in $G$, giving the asserted identification of functors, not just of objects. The equivalence extends to constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves simply by retaining the $\Lambda$-actions: an action on a pair is a pair of actions, and a map is $\Lambda$-linear exactly when both components are. Therefore $t_!J$ is injective as a module sheaf. Indeed a monomorphism becomes $(M_A,M_W)\hookrightarrow(N_A,N_W)$ componentwise. A map from its source to $(J,0)$ is $(u,0)$; injectivity of $J$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] extends $u$ to $N_A\to J$, and pairing that extension with the zero map on $N_W$ gives the required lift.

source.place: Tag 03S5 (proposition-describe-jshriek); finite clopen decomposition in Tag 0A5B (lemma-constant-smooth-statements), proof first paragraph; componentwise injective lifting written out

proof.text: The complex consisting of the injective module sheaf $t_!J$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere is a bounded-below complex of injectives. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], applying the additive direct image $s_*$ to this complex computes $Rs_*(t_!J)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. It still has only degree zero, so $R^qs_*(t_!J)=0$ for $q>0$. The comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison] then gives $R^qs_*((t_!J)_{ab})=0$ as well.

Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-assembly] to the Cartesian square defining $V$, the proper map $p$, and the torsion abelian sheaf $F_{ab}$. It gives $i^{-1}R^qp_*F_{ab}\cong R^qs_*b^{-1}F_{ab}$. The base change of $k$ along $b$ has source $A\times_B V\cong A$, since $pk$ factors through the open $C$; its open immersion is precisely $t$. Extension-by-zero base change [sbc-prop-extension-by-zero-and-arbitrary-base-change] therefore gives $b^{-1}F\cong t_!J$, and the same identity on underlying abelian sheaves. Step 4 proves $i^{-1}R^qp_*F_{ab}=0$ for $q>0$. For every geometric point of $D$ whose image is in $C$, its lift to the open $C$ consequently has zero stalk of this sheaf; equivalently its pullback to that point is zero [lem-kun-stalks-of-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 095T (theorem-proper-base-change), as stated degreewise in lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-assembly; Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change); Tag 0DDF (lemma-proper-base-change-stalk)

proof.text: Let $\bar d:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to D$ be a geometric point with image outside $i(C)$, and put $B_{\bar d}=B\times_D\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, with projection $a:B_{\bar d}\to B$ and proper map $p_{\bar d}:B_{\bar d}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The base change of $k$ along $a$ has source $A\times_D\operatorname{Spec}\Omega=\varnothing$: any point in it would, by $pk=ir$, give a lift of $\bar d$ to $C$, which is impossible. By [sbc-prop-extension-by-zero-and-arbitrary-base-change], $a^{-1}F_{ab}$ is the extension of a sheaf on the empty scheme, hence zero (the empty cover forces every section of such an abelian sheaf to be zero). Proper base change [lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-assembly] now gives $\bar d^{-1}R^qp_*F_{ab}\cong R^qp_{\bar d,*}(0)=0$; the last equality follows also directly by applying direct image to the zero injective complex [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. This is exactly vanishing of the geometric stalk by [lem-kun-stalks-of-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), case (b), geometric-fibre argument; Etale Cohomology Tags 03S6 and 0DDF

proof.text: Steps 5 and 6 cover every geometric point of $D$. Thus the map $0\to R^qp_*F_{ab}$ is an isomorphism at every geometric stalk for each $q>0$, so it is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison] identifies this zero sheaf with the underlying abelian sheaf of the module higher direct image $R^qp_*F$. A module whose underlying abelian sheaf is zero has only zero sections and is the zero module sheaf. Hence $R^qp_*(k_!J)=0$.
